# Inia AI Documentation

> The documentation of Inia AI, the platform that turns a set of documents into a written report. Each link is a Markdown file, as a path from the root of this repository.

Frontmatter on every page carries `type`, `status` and a `description` that says what the page holds and when to read it. Pages with `status: planned` describe designs, not behavior. Pages under Research document external systems, not the platform.

## Getting Started
- [Platform Overview](docs/getting-started/platform-overview.md): Says what the platform does for an outside reader: who it is for, what a run produces, its parts, and the model accounts it needs. Read when you meet the platform for the first time, or need to say in a few lines what it does.
- [Quickstart](docs/getting-started/quickstart.md): Takes a reader from a clone of the open repository to a report whose figures link to their pages, with the one-command Docker stack and the sample workflows, then checks the result from the command line. Read when you run the open edition for the first time, or want to see a run end to end.
- [Upgrade to a New Release](docs/getting-started/upgrade.md): Says what the platform does to its database each time it starts, and moves an install of the open repository from one release to the next: back up the database, check out the new release tag, rebuild, check the migration, and roll back by restoring the backup. Read when you upgrade an install, plan a rollback, or want to know why a start changed the database.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/getting-started/troubleshooting.md): Lists the failures that a first start, a sample run and the command-line check have met, each with what you see, the cause and the fix: a full disk during the build, a port in use, a setting that did not take, a first admin who cannot sign in, a sample missing from the app, the agent sample failing on Ubuntu, a block skipped for want of a Cohere key, and each FAIL line of the check. Read when the stack does not start, a sample run fails, or the check prints FAIL.
- [The Open Build and the Full Edition](docs/getting-started/editions.md): Lists, area by area, what the open build of the platform holds and what the full edition adds, and what the open build does when it meets a part of the full edition. Read when you need to know whether a feature, a block or a document format is in the open build.
- [Security of an Install](docs/getting-started/security.md): Lists what to set before an install of the platform serves real users, and says how sign-in, roles, the separation of organizations and documents that carry instructions work. Read when you prepare an install for production, need the rules for passwords, second factors, roles or organizations, or check that a run does not obey a document.
- [Solution Layout](docs/getting-started/solution-layout.md): Maps the Clean Architecture layers to the actual project folders and files of the platform solution, project by project, with a where-does-X-live lookup, the test and support projects and the build output. Read when you look for where a kind of code lives in IniaAi.Platform or add a project.
- [Docker Builds](docs/getting-started/docker-builds.md): Walks through the one command that builds and starts the whole product, building the platform's three Docker images from their recipes, running one, the corporate proxy settings chart rendering needs, and reading the logs. Read when you build or run a platform image on your own machine, or an image build or a container start fails.
- [The Docker Stack](docs/getting-started/docker-stack.md): Describes the Docker build of the open repository and its one-command stack: the images and their recipes, the services of compose.yaml, how the secrets reach each service, the agent runtime's sandbox settings, and the compose check. Read when you change the Docker build or the stack, a service of the stack does not start, or you need to know where a secret lives.

## Contributing
- [C# Code Standards](docs/getting-started/csharp-code-standards.md): Reference of the C# house rules: naming, mandatory braces, layout, test rules, API contracts and DTO mapping, EF Core entity configuration, comments, logging and validators. Read when you write or review platform C# code.
- [Writing Messages for Users](docs/getting-started/user-messages.md): The rules for a message that a person reads: an error, a refusal reason, a notice or a run log line. It names the readers, gives each rule with its published source, and shows messages before and after the rules. Read when you write or change any text that the apps or the API show to a user.
- [Testing](docs/getting-started/testing.md): Describes the platform's CI test run, the test runner, the rules that keep tests fast, reading a red run, the opt-in for tests that call paid APIs, the local database-backed integration tests, and editor-app component tests with bUnit. Read when you write, run or debug a platform test, or a CI test run fails.
- [Database Migrations](docs/getting-started/database-migrations.md): Walks through creating, cleaning up and applying EF Core migrations for the Core and UserData contexts on both providers with the migration script, how startup applies them, and how to squash them into one InitialCreate. Read when you change an entity and need a migration, a migration is empty, conflicting or missing on one provider, or you squash the migrations.

## Overview
- [Overview (overview)](docs/architecture/index.md): Top-level architecture hub linking to every architecture subsection: layers and containers, the workflow engine, documents, AI, tenancy, services, jobs and provenance. Read when you look for how a part of the platform works and do not yet know which page owns it.

## Foundations
- [Clean Architecture](docs/architecture/clean-architecture/index.md): The platform's layer split (Domain, Application, Core, Infrastructure, the two hosts and the supporting projects), the real project references between them, CQRS through the in-house dispatcher, the specification repositories and units of work, where services are registered, and how tests stand up the layers. Read when you decide which project new code belongs in, or need the shape of a command, a query or a repository call.
- [Platform Tour](docs/architecture/platform-tour.md): Describes the open build in one page: its parts, its projects and their layers, and the path of a run from the upload of a document to a report with cited figures, with the class that does each step. Read when you are new to the code and want to find your way through the projects, or follow a run through the platform.
- [C4 Model](docs/architecture/c4-model/index.md): Hub page for the C4 model, linking to the system context/container diagram and per-subsystem component docs. Read when you look for the platform's architecture diagrams.
- [System Context & Containers](docs/architecture/c4-model/container.md): C4 system-context and container diagrams of the platform: its users, the external systems it calls, and each container (Vue SPA, REST API, Blazor admin app, agent runtime, the two databases, file storage) with its technology and what it talks to. Read when you need the platform's moving parts on one page, or which process does what.

## Workflow Engine
- [Overview](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/index.md): Explains the Workflow-Section-Block hierarchy and the key properties of each level, separator sections, how a run is scheduled and where its documents come from, and links to each engine subsystem page. Read when you need the shape of a workflow template or a map of the workflow engine pages.
- [Workflow Types & Categories](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/workflow-types.md): Documents workflow types and their categories, the reserved and module types, which organizations may use a type (WorkflowTypeOrganizationAccess) and where that is and is not checked, the Workflow Type Management page with its tenant dialog, creating a type through the template API, duplicating a type, and deleting one through the API. Read when you add, duplicate, delete or grant a workflow type, or need to know who can see or run one.
- [Block Strategy Pattern](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/block-strategy-pattern.md): Documents the IBlockStrategy interface, every BlockExecutionContext service and run field, how open and module strategies are registered, placeholder substitution and sanitization, the strategy catalog and the agent family, and how to test a strategy. Read when you write or change a block strategy, or need to know what a strategy can reach at run time.
- [ExaSearch Block](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/exa-search-block.md): Documents the Intelligent Search block's Exa integration: the ExaSettings configuration, the strategy's execution flow and failure handling, every IntelligentSearchProperties field, the XML-tagged output, and the document it can create. Read when you configure or debug an Intelligent Search block or change the Exa integration.
- [Block Implementation Guide](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/block-implementation-guide.md): Step-by-step guide for adding a new workflow block type, in the platform or in a project of its own: the type number, the typed properties and execution state, the catalog definition, the strategy and its registration, the editor component, label and hue, the extension setting, what happens to a block whose type is not installed, and the tests that prove it round-trips and runs. Read when you add a block type or a block type fails to load, save or appear in the editor.
- [Editor State Model](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/editor-state-model.md): Explains the Blazor editor's EditorSurfaceState container and its events, the EditorSurfaceCapabilities flags, how one section editing unit is reused by the full editor and the Component Library, the editor's Library and transfer gestures, the Library link index behind the badges, accents and reconcile drawer, and the rendering model. Read when you change the workflow editor or the Component Library, or a Library badge or reconcile row looks wrong.
- [Shared Components](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/shared-components.md): Explains the shared-components data model and its API surface: the Core registry and version chain, the link record carried by blocks and sections, the hash-vs-payload canonicalization split, promote/materialize, the reconcile loop with atomic fan-out, composable sections with per-entry overrides, definition writes and restore, retire/unretire, categories, cross-deployment transfer, and the agent-facing guards. Read when you work on the Library, a SharedComponent.* error, a reconcile decision, or moving a workflow type between deployments.
- [Execution Context](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/execution-context.md): Explains a workflow run from the job's side and the handler's side: the job steps before the handler (execution row, anonymisation, email intake, run input stage, document processing), the handler's phases, the SharedInputs dictionary and what a block strategy receives, when a block or section is skipped, and how a block failure is recorded. Read when you trace what happens between a submission and a finished report, or why a block was skipped or failed.
- [Variable System](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/variable-system.md): Documents the WorkflowVariable entity, the reserved, variable and block replacement tags and how each is substituted, duplicate-tag handling, run-time value validation, and confidential variables. Read when you add a variable, write a {tag} in a prompt, see a duplicate-tag warning, or a run is refused for a variable value.
- [Parallel DAG Execution](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/parallel-execution.md): Documents the whole-workflow parallel DAG scheduler: dispatch segments, graph building, layering, barriers and fences, the per-run concurrency cap, the per-block pooled writer, how a persistence failure, a critical block or a fence ends the run, cycle breaking, verification group shape, and signature-override injection. Read when blocks run in an unexpected order, a run fails with ResultsLost, CriticalBlockFailure or VerificationGroupShape, or you change how blocks are dispatched.
- [Loop Processing](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/loop-processing.md): Explains how a LoopStart/LoopEnd pair is expanded at run time: resolving the list, one loop item block plus a clone of the body per item, tag and placeholder rewriting, per-iteration counterparty data, the database sync, and what happens when the list is empty or a loop is malformed. Read when you build a loop, a loop runs the wrong number of times, or a {ListTitle} reference resolves to no data.
- [Parameterized Sections](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/parameterized-sections.md): Explains how a parameterized section expands into one copy per variant at run time: the config model, what each copy gets, tag suffixing and params, the ClassMap that rewrites document classes per variant, document distribution, the legacy-config conversion, the class rename/delete cascade, and the editor dialog. Read when you configure a parameterized section, a variant reads the wrong documents or tags, or you add a field to SectionVariant.
- [Object Cloning Patterns](docs/architecture/workflow-engine/object-cloning-patterns.md): Explains how workflow entities clone: the CloneHelper.CopyScalars copy modes, the three-phase clone methods of Workflow, Section and Block, when to mark a property [CloneIgnore], how ExecutionState is shared, and the gotchas. Read when you add a field or an entity to a workflow template, or a field goes missing after a duplicate, an execution or an upload.

## Multi-Tenancy
- [Overview](docs/architecture/multi-tenant/index.md): Overview of multi-tenancy inside one deployment: the organization as tenant, membership and roles, how a request gets its tenant, what is shared and what is per organization, the one deliberate cross-tenant read, how organizations are created and deactivated, and the audit records. Read when you need the tenancy model before touching data access, or look for which multi-tenant page owns a detail.
- [Security Model](docs/architecture/multi-tenant/security-model.md): The layered security model behind multi-tenant isolation: transport, OpenIddict authentication and its flows, tenant resolution and membership checks, data-access scoping, the threat model, tests, encryption and audit. Read when you assess how one organization is kept from another's data, or change authentication or the tenant checks.
- [Data Isolation](docs/architecture/multi-tenant/data-isolation.md): Where organization isolation is enforced: storage buckets, the OrganizationId column and its foreign keys, explicit scoping in handlers (and why there is no global tenant query filter), the API's tenant checks, the admin app's tenant switch and by-id reads, shared templates, and the isolation tests. Read when you write a query over tenant data, add a by-id read, or check how a cross-organization read is refused.
- [Database Design](docs/architecture/multi-tenant/database-design.md): The CoreDbContext/UserDataDbContext split and what each holds, the entities they share, the key relationships, template access by join, the soft-delete filter as the only global filter, the tenant descriptor, and how migrations run at startup. Read when you decide which context an entity belongs to, or need how templates and tenant data relate.
- [API Architecture](docs/architecture/multi-tenant/api-architecture.md): The API's tenant and authentication pipeline: the X-Tenant-Id header, the five middleware layers and their order, why tenant rejection runs before token validation, the exact 403 responses, excluded paths, and how controllers and handlers receive the organization. Read when an API call fails with 403 Tenant context required or Invalid tenant context, or when you add an endpoint and need its tenant handling.
- [Deployment](docs/architecture/multi-tenant/deployment.md): The processes one deployment runs (API, admin app, Vue SPA behind nginx, agent runtime, databases, object storage), what is not there (no Redis, no separate job worker), the health endpoints and every health check. Read when you need what a deployment consists of, or what /health and /readiness report.
- [Risk Assessment](docs/architecture/multi-tenant/risk-assessment.md): Catalogs multi-tenant isolation risks and their mitigations, e.g. tenant forgery, missed query scoping, cross-tenant template exposure, and the accepted residual items. Read when you assess a change's isolation risk or review what isolation leaves to convention.

## AI Integration
- [Overview](docs/architecture/ai-integration/index.md): Hub page pointing to the AI providers/connectors page and its Azure integration companion pages. Read when you look for where the platform's model calls, provider selection or provider auth are documented.
- [Providers & Connectors](docs/architecture/ai-integration/providers.md): How the platform reaches Claude and Cohere: the chat and embeddings connector chosen per deployment, the auth per backend, the AiModel ids, model routing per stack, thinking and effort request shapes, refusals, rate limiting and retries. Read when you configure a deployment's models or provider, debug a model call that fails, or add a model to the catalogue.
- [Azure AI Foundry](docs/architecture/ai-integration/azure-foundry.md): The Azure AI Foundry deployment mode: the two endpoints, the auth headers and Entra ID scope, the config keys, the Foundry models and quota to provision, and the agent path in Azure mode (allowlist shape check, model id normalisation, azure-foundry pricing rows). Read when you deploy the platform on Azure or debug an Azure-mode model call, allowlist refusal or cost.
- [Azure Platform Integration](docs/architecture/ai-integration/azure-platform-integration.md): How the platform code talks to Azure AI Foundry: the Azure branch of AnthropicChatConnector, the AzureCohereEmbeddingsConnector request translation, error parsing, DI wiring, the AzureFoundrySettings keys, Entra ID auth and the construction-time checks. Read when you change or debug the Azure code path.

## RAG
- [RAG Services](docs/architecture/rag/index.md): The end-to-end RAG pipeline from upload to cited answer, every retrieval strategy (RagTypes) and how it selects pages, how vector ranking works, and how retrieved pages reach the model. Read when a block retrieves the wrong pages, or you choose or change a retrieval strategy.
- [Chunking](docs/architecture/rag/chunking.md): Page-grouping chunking for AI Query blocks: when it runs, the fixed-count and bin-packing chunkers, the table-of-contents case, the 100-image cap per request, and the settings' trade-offs. Read when a block runs once per batch of pages, or you set its chunking properties.
- [Overview Generation](docs/architecture/rag/overview-generation.md): How each page's AI overview (the text that gets embedded) is generated: the sliding window, the prompt resolution from the workflow, the model, what is stored and when it is invalidated, token accounting, diagnosing a bad or missing overview, and the migration from the Prompt Library. Read when a page has no overview or a poor one, retrieval misses a page, or you change overview prompts.
- [Embedding Generation](docs/architecture/rag/embedding-generation.md): How page overviews become vectors: which pages are embedded, the batching, the Cohere connector chosen per deployment, the model and dimension, the stored EmbeddingVector with its error sentinel, token accounting, and what a deployment without a Cohere key does. Read when pages are not embedded or retrieval finds nothing, or a block names the Cohere key, or you change the embeddings model.

## Document Processing
- [Document Processing](docs/architecture/document-processing/index.md): The file-format interface the platform reads and writes documents through, its free implementation in the open build, the PDFium worker process, the format handlers (PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, plain text, images, email), the counted pages of an upload, the page-image DPI budget, and the password unlock gate. Read when you change how a document format is read or written, or debug a document that fails to page, render or unlock.
- [Replace a File-Format Implementation](docs/architecture/document-processing/file-formats.md): Names the document interfaces of the platform and their contracts, the free implementation the open build registers, how the PDFium worker process sandboxes itself, and how to put your own implementation in place of one format or of all of them and check it. Read when you replace or add a document format implementation, or check the PDF worker's sandbox.
- [File Content Inspection](docs/architecture/document-processing/file-content-inspector.md): The byte-level file inspector: what it detects, what it admits, what it refuses, which limits it enforces, where it runs, and how a check is added. Read when an upload or an email part is refused, or when you add an intake check or a format the platform reads.
- [OCR](docs/architecture/ocr/index.md): The model-based OCR pipeline: page render at the model's long edge, one-shot transcription, the (disabled) fidelity judge, per-page outcomes and refusals, image routing, prompts, model choice, OcrSettings, token recording, the page-quality checks that send a page to OCR, and troubleshooting. Read when a page's text is missing, wrong, refused or routed as an image, or when you tune OCR cost, memory or model.
- [Chart Rendering](docs/architecture/chart-rendering/index.md): How a Dynamic Chart block becomes a chart: the strategy's ChartConfiguration, the shared ECharts options builder that draws it in the Vue app and, bundled, in the Word export's headless-Chromium PNG, chart types and colours, ChartRenderingSettings, the ChromeDriver pool, the table fallback, the bundle copy in the platform, and the ECharts update procedure. Read when a chart looks wrong in the app or in a Word export, or when you change the chart builder or the ECharts version.
- [File Storage](docs/architecture/file-storage/index.md): The file storage layer: the Database and MinIO providers (S3 implemented, not registered), bucket naming and the fixed-bucket on-premise mode, provider resolution and its fallback, the FileMetadata and Files rows, storage categories, the Database-to-MinIO migration, blob deletion, and the MinIO proxy issue. Read when you configure where a deployment stores files, move files between providers, or debug a file that cannot be read back.

## Application & Services Layer
- [Overview](docs/architecture/services/index.md): Overview of the services layer: the application, core and infrastructure service categories, where services are registered and with which lifetimes, the repository, unit-of-work and strategy patterns, and the cross-cutting concerns. Read when you look for where a service lives or is registered, before the page that owns its detail.
- [Service Registration](docs/architecture/services/service-registration.md): Service lifetimes with real examples, the keyed, conditional, options and factory registration patterns, and how a closed module registers its services. Read when you choose a lifetime for a new service or debug a scoped/singleton mismatch.
- [Dependency Injection](docs/architecture/services/dependency-injection.md): The DI registration entry points of each layer and host, and the registration patterns in use (keyed storage and workflow handlers, conditional connectors, options). Read when you register a new service or look for where an existing one is registered.
- [Command Handlers](docs/architecture/services/application/command-handlers.md): The CQRS command-handler shape: the request record, the handler, the in-house dispatcher and its two dispatch paths, the validation step, and ErrorOr error handling. Read when you add or change a command, or a command's error does not reach the caller as expected.
- [Query Handlers](docs/architecture/services/application/query-handlers.md): The CQRS query-handler shape and its reads through Ardalis specifications and projections. Read when you add or change a query, or a read is slow or returns another organization's rows.
- [Validation Services](docs/architecture/services/application/validation-services.md): The FluentValidation step the in-house dispatcher runs before a handler, how validators are found, and the validator conventions. Read when a request is refused with a validation error, or you write a validator.
- [Database Services](docs/architecture/services/infrastructure/database-services.md): The two EF Core DbContexts, the dual-provider setup, the transient-fault retry policy and what it demands of explicit transactions, the repositories and units of work, and how migrations and seeding run at startup. Read when you open a transaction, update an entity, add a migration, or debug a startup migration or a retried command.
- [Email Services](docs/architecture/services/infrastructure/email-services.md): SMTP, SendGrid and Amazon SES IEmailSender providers behind IOutgoingMail, which picks one at startup and turns mail on only when that provider is fully configured; its senders are the password reset, the second-factor code, the admin app's account mail and any a closed module adds; no workflow-related email exists. Read when mail does not arrive, when you configure a mail provider, or when someone asks whether the platform emails about workflows.
- [File Services](docs/architecture/services/infrastructure/file-services.md): The keyed file-storage backends (Database, MinIO; S3 not wired), their resolver and manager, and the MinIO health check. Read when you need which storage services are registered and how one is chosen; the storage design itself is on File Storage.
- [Agent Runtime Integration](docs/architecture/services/infrastructure/agent-runtime-integration.md): The shared agent-integration layer: one executor owning start → gated poll → collect → persist → acknowledge-or-withhold, session-bundle custody, the failure-absorbing policies and their cost, billing from trace tokens, run fuses, the poll gate, 503 handling, the request-repair helpers, agent conversations, registration, and the consumers. Read when an agent-family block or an editor agent turn fails, stalls, retries or costs more than expected, or when you build a new consumer of the agent runtime.

## Background Jobs
- [Background Jobs Service](docs/architecture/background-jobs/index.md): The in-memory JobsService that runs workflow executions and editor agent turns: job types and states, the queue and the parallel path, the concurrency caps, cancellation, the shutdown drain, what a restart loses, and the exact log lines for a stuck or failed job. Read when you trace a report run that is stuck, failed or lost after a restart, or tune MaxConcurrentJobs.

## Citations & Provenance
- [Citations](docs/architecture/citations/index.md): The citations pipeline from a model's or web search's cited text to the <fact> markers and citations of a report paragraph: which blocks are citation sources, source types, fact extraction, quantity- and date-aware matching, source expansion and flattening, block citations, citations to the block that produced a figure, citation traces, and the citation regression test. Read when a report figure is unmarked, wrongly linked or cites the wrong page, or when you change citation matching.
- [Web Search Citations](docs/architecture/citations/web-search-citations.md): How a Web API Call block's response from Perplexity or Parallel.ai is detected by URL, parsed into (claim, sources) pairs and turned into grounded citation facts by CitationFactBuilder, with the fallbacks and the tests. Read when a Perplexity or Parallel.ai answer shows no citations or cites the wrong link.
- [Tracer Agent (Graph RAG)](docs/architecture/tracer-agent/index.md): The Tracer Agent: provenance questions about a run's output answered from a graph of the run's blocks, inputs and documents, how the graph is built and cached, the BFS traversal and its limits, the node kinds, the API, and the fact that no screen calls it today. Read when you work on run provenance, the graph endpoints, or the Graph RAG prompts.

## Frontend (Vue SPA)
- [Overview](docs/architecture/frontend/index.md): Overview of the Vue 3 SPA: its tech stack, repository layout, bootstrap flow, local dev quickstart and the desk preview page. Read when you start work in the Vue app or need to know which library or folder owns a concern.
- [API Service Layer](docs/architecture/frontend/api-layer.md): Documents the frontend API service layer: BaseService, its interceptors, the per-domain triad, the API singleton, error messages, OData, timestamps, file transfer and the inventory of every service module. Read when you add or change a call to the platform API from the Vue app, or need to know which frontend module calls an endpoint.
- [Components & Design System](docs/architecture/frontend/components-and-design-system.md): Documents the Atomic Design component layering, the reka-ui/shadcn pattern and its keyboard behaviour, Tailwind v4 and the design tokens, status colours and pills, the workflow-state mapping, the execution log page, the report's document panel, icons, the theme and the brand marks. Read when you add or restyle a component, pick a colour token, change the header, the theme, the execution log or the report panel, or need to know where a component belongs.
- [Forms, Tables & Composables](docs/architecture/frontend/forms-tables-and-composables.md): Documents the VeeValidate and Zod form pattern, the TanStack table column factories with their row-control guard, the composables inventory and where shared types and enums live. Read when you add or change a form, a table or a composable in the Vue app, or look for an existing composable before writing one.
- [State, Routing & Auth](docs/architecture/frontend/state-routing-and-auth.md): Documents the four Pinia stores, the Vue Router with its public routes, guard order and role gating, the JWT and refresh-token lifecycle, the login, 2FA and external sign-in flows, the tenant header and the route table. Read when you add or gate a route, change sign-in or token handling, or need to know which role reaches a screen of the Vue app.
- [Charts](docs/architecture/frontend/charts.md): Documents how the Vue app draws charts with Apache ECharts: the registration module, the shared buildChartOptions builder of block charts, the BaseChart component and its themes, the chart bundle the Word export loads with its freshness check and the platform's copy of it, and how a report paragraph becomes a chart. Read when you change a chart type, the chart option logic or the ECharts version, or a block chart renders differently in the app and in the Word export.
- [Real-time & Polling](docs/architecture/frontend/realtime-and-polling.md): Documents that the Vue app learns of run progress by polling with TanStack Query, lists every poll and its interval, and states that there is no live push: the SignalR hub and its client were removed. Read when a screen does not update while a run is in flight, you add a poll, or you consider live push.
- [Internationalization](docs/architecture/frontend/i18n.md): Documents the vue-i18n setup of the Vue app: the configuration, the locale tree and module copy, interpolation and pluralization, the escaping rules and the tests that guard them. Read when you add or change user-facing text in IniaAi.Web or a locale test fails.
- [Testing](docs/architecture/frontend/testing.md): Documents the Vue app's Vitest stack and config, the colocated-test convention, the shared setup (Storage polyfill, auto-unmount, scrolling stubs), every shared test helper, where tests exist and the discipline expected. Read when you write or debug a frontend test, or look for an existing helper before writing one.
- [Build & Deployment](docs/architecture/frontend/build-and-deploy.md): Documents the Vite build and its chunks, the npm scripts, the build-time environment variables, the stale-chunk reload, and the nginx Docker image with its proxy target and routes. Read when you change the frontend build, an environment variable, the web image or its nginx config, or debug a deployed SPA that cannot reach the API.

## Frontend — Features & Guides
- [Signatures & Overrides](docs/architecture/frontend/signatures.md): Documents the signature-override screens of the Vue app: the routes and their role gate, the picker with its review pills, the four-column editor and its per-field proposal and vote flow, the signatures API hooks, the test-replay playground and the history tab. Read when you change how a tenant proposes, reviews or tests a signature field override in the Vue app.
- [Documents: Upload & Viewer](docs/architecture/frontend/document-handling.md): Documents the Vue app's document screens: the list with its upload and edit dialogs, the detail page and page reader, the category screen, the run uploader's upload composable, the PDF and image previews, media-type grouping and the documents, files and pages API modules. Read when you change how the Vue app lists, uploads, previews, edits or downloads documents.
- [Rich Text Editor (TipTap)](docs/architecture/frontend/rich-text-editor.md): Documents the TipTap v3 rich-text editor of report paragraphs: where it is used, its v-model contract, keyboard and screen-reader behaviour, extensions, the toolbar, and how an edit keeps the citations, card layouts, tables and lists the report wrote. Read when you change paragraph editing, an edit loses markup or a citation, or you add an editor extension.
- [Notifications & Errors](docs/architecture/frontend/notifications-and-errors.md): Documents the shared toast system of the Vue app, its variants and one-toast limit, and how an API failure reaches a component and the user. Read when you show success or failure feedback in a new screen, or a toast or an error message does not appear as expected.
- [Source Chain & Citations](docs/architecture/frontend/source-chain-and-citations.md): Documents how the Vue app renders and sanitises report content, the citation data model, the fact popover and its keyboard behaviour, the source-chain drill-down panel and the unmounted tracer dialog. Read when you change how citations, fact markers or sanitised HTML show in a report, or a citation's sources do not appear.
- [Adding a Feature (guide)](docs/architecture/frontend/contributing-a-feature.md): Step-by-step guide to adding a CRUD feature to the Vue app end to end: API module, store, form, table, view and route, navigation, i18n, tests and the local gate. Read when you add a new screen or resource to IniaAi.Web and want the order of the layers and the registration steps that make it reachable.

## Guides
- [Guides (overview)](docs/guides/index.md): Hub of the guides: the quickstart, the end-to-end journeys, workflow and block guides, reading a report, and page overview prompts. Read when you want a task-oriented walkthrough and do not know which guide covers it.

## End-to-end Task Guides
- [Overview — I want to…](docs/guides/end-to-end/index.md): Hub of numbered end-to-end journeys by goal — build a workflow, integrate against the API, debug retrieval or a stuck job, add a block or frontend feature — and the contract every journey follows. Read when you start cold and need the whole sequence of steps for one goal.
- [Build Your First Workflow](docs/guides/end-to-end/build-your-first-workflow.md): Walks a prompt engineer through building a first workflow type with a Retrieve Data From Documents block and an AI Query block that reads its pages, running it from the editor, and reading the report. Read when you build your first workflow in the editor.
- [API: Zero to Result](docs/guides/end-to-end/api-zero-to-result.md): Walks an API integrator from a system user through a token, discovery, a one-call submit, polling, reading the report tree, and resolving a citation to its source. Read when you wire an external service to the REST API for the first time.
- [Debug Retrieval](docs/guides/end-to-end/debug-retrieval.md): Diagnostic runbook for a wrong-page citation: shows what a block retrieved, then walks the retrieval strategy, batching, page overviews and citation matching to the one setting to change. Read when a report cites the wrong page, misses a fact that is in the document, or pulls in an irrelevant page.
- [Debug a Stuck Job](docs/guides/end-to-end/debug-stuck-job.md): Diagnostic runbook for a workflow run that never finishes: reads the job's state and progress, then tells queued-behind-the-cap, slow, stalled and lost-on-restart apart and names what to do for each. Read when a run spins on the Dashboard, a report never appears, or a job id returns 404.

## Workflows
- [Overview](docs/guides/workflows/index.md): Hub for authoring workflows: links to the editor guide, the first-workflow walkthrough, document classes, overview prompts, reading a report, and the architecture pages behind variables, tags, loops, retrieval and models. Read when you are about to author or change a workflow and need the page that covers one part of it.
- [Workflow Editor Guide](docs/guides/workflows/editor-guide.md): Full walkthrough of the workflow editor: creating a type, sections, blocks, variables, saving and version history, import and export, test runs and Generate Report, re-arranging, and the dependency chain and Graph tab. Read when you build or change a workflow in the editor and need to know where a control is or what it does.
- [Document Classes](docs/guides/workflows/document-classes.md): How to define, edit, and delete a workflow's document classes in the editor, point each block at the classes it reads, and what the pre-run check refuses or warns about, with its exact messages. Read when you add a document class, a block reads the wrong documents, or a run is refused for a missing or extra document.
- [Run a Report in the Web App](docs/guides/workflows/run-a-report.md): Walks an analyst through running a report in the Vue app: Create New Report, choosing the report type, uploading and classifying the documents, the company and parameters, the review, and following the run until its report opens. Read when you run a report for the first time, or a step of Create New Report asks for something you do not have.
- [Reading a Report](docs/guides/workflows/reading-a-report.md): How to find, read, and export a finished report in IniaAi.Web: the report list and its status labels, the report's sections, tracing a citation to its source page, checking the JSON data a run sends to other systems, and the Actions menu. Read when you open a run's report, wonder what its status means, check a run's data output, or need to export or re-run it.

## Page Overviews
- [Page Overview Prompts](docs/guides/page-overview-prompts.md): How to set a workflow's page overview prompts on the workflow editor's Document Classes tab: the default, a class's own prompt, the one-page version, and the warning for blocks that search pages a class never summarises. Read when a search step finds nothing in a document class, the Document Classes tab warns about page overviews, or you write an overview prompt.

## Block Catalog
- [Overview](docs/guides/blocks/index.md): Hub for workflow blocks: what a block is, the block types by category with a link to each one's reference entry, and the architecture and feature guides behind them. Read when you are choosing a block type or looking for the page that documents one.
- [Block Reference](docs/guides/blocks/block-reference.md): Complete configuration reference for every workflow block type: the settings each editor shows with their defaults, what each block outputs, how it fails, the Agent block, the blocks only the paid build runs, and the placeholder system with substituted-value sanitization. Read when you configure a block, a block's output or error surprises you, or you write a {tag} that reads another block.
- [Add a Block Type](docs/guides/blocks/add-a-block-type.md): Builds a block type in its own project, step by step, on the Count Words example: the settings, the execution state, the strategy, the editor, the extension, how to load it from source and in the Docker stack, and the tests that cover it. Read when you add a block type without a change to the platform, or an install meets a block whose extension it lacks.
- [AI Query Output Format](docs/guides/blocks/ai-query-output-format.md): Walks through configuring an AI Query block's Output Format (named tags, JSON, JSON in a tag): the Simple Schema Builder and Advanced JSON Schema, the lenient validator, the exact error messages, the one retry, and how later blocks read the extracted values. Read when you need a later block to read one value out of an AI Query answer, or an AI Query block fails output-format validation.
- [Web Search Citations](docs/guides/blocks/web-search-citations.md): Walks through configuring a Web API Call block against Perplexity or Parallel.ai so the answer's web sources become clickable report citations: the endpoints that trigger it, the block settings, the stored-key header, and what makes a citation appear. Read when you want cited web research in a report, or a Perplexity or Parallel.ai block produces no citations.
- [Communication Blocks (Planned)](docs/guides/blocks/communication-blocks.md): Describes the planned Email Send and Webhook Call blocks, which do not exist (no such block type), and how to call a webhook today with a Web API Call block. Read when you need a workflow to send an email or call a webhook.

## Overview
- [Overview (overview)](docs/features/index.md): Features hub linking to every feature page: workflow management, documents, and user management and access, with pointers to the architecture pages. Read when you look for how a user-facing feature behaves and do not yet know which page owns it.

## Workflow Management
- [Template Versioning](docs/features/workflow-template-versioning.md): Explains the append-only, content-hashed workflow template version history: how a save records a version and when it dedups, the version table, saving and reading history over the API with its 409 and error codes, duplicating a template into a new type, the editor agent's version note, the editor's history and conflict dialog, cross-deployment currency cards, and payload retention. Read when you save, restore, compare or duplicate a workflow template, or a save answers 409.
- [Editor Agent](docs/features/editor-agent.md): Agent mode in the workflow editor: how to open it, what the agent does (answers, reads past reports and report feedback, proposes changes, model choice, workflow notes), how a proposal is reviewed and saved, what it never does, how a deployment switches it on, and its cost and daily spend limit. Read when you use or support Agent mode in the workflow editor, or a proposal cannot be accepted.
- [Editor Agent Evals](docs/features/editor-agent-evals.md): How to run the editor agent's eval set against a live agent runtime, what its 23 cases check, how each is graded, and where the results and cost are written. Read when you change the editor agent's guidance, staged files or model, or need to run or read the evals.
- [GitHub Save](docs/features/workflow-github-save.md): Explains how workflow templates are mirrored to a GitHub repository through the GitHub Contents API: the four paths that commit, the commit identity, the GitHubSettings keys and where they live, how to create and rotate the PAT, and the errors and logs. Read when you set up or debug the GitHub mirror of workflow templates, or its token expires.
- [Tools Settings](docs/features/tools-settings.md): The prompt sets on the admin app's Tools Settings page: what each tab holds, which step reads it, when an edit takes effect, and how a deployment gets its first copy. Read when you change a deployment-wide prompt outside a workflow's blocks, such as the Excel analysis, Build Topics or OCR prompts.
- [Signature Field Overrides](docs/features/signature-overrides.md): Explains per-organization signature field overrides: workflow-level field definitions, the override table, the propose, vote and promote review queue, the audit log, how renames and deletions carry through a template save, the SignatureContributor role, the API and the replay playground. Read when you work on signature fields or overrides, or a client's override does not reach a block.
- [Documents from Blocks](docs/features/docs-from-blocks.md): Explains how a block creates a document during a run: which block does (Intelligent Search), how the document is stored, paged and added to the run's pages, how CreatesDocumentClass targets it at later blocks, and which outputs are never paged. Read when a later block should read what an earlier block produced, or a created document does not reach a block.
- [Report Feedback](docs/features/report-feedback.md): Explains report feedback: where a reader leaves it on a finished report, who may list, delete, triage and read it across organizations, what an item records and its limits, its Open, Addressed and Dismissed lifecycle, and its storage. Read when you work on report feedback, triage it, or the editor agent's Use feedback.

## Documents
- [Documents Screen](docs/features/document-management/screen-guide.md): Walks through uploading, processing, marking static, and reading each page beside its original on the Documents pages, and how to have a document read again. Read when you upload documents outside a workflow, inspect what the platform read from a page, or need a document's text read afresh.
- [Page Image API — Frontend](docs/features/document-management/page-image-api-integration-on-frontend.md): How the Vue app loads the image the platform renders for a document page: the PageService client, the usePageImage composable with its error copy and object-URL handling, the page preview dialog a cited page opens, and the page reader's original panel. Read when you work on page previews, a preview shows an error, or you add a new place that shows a page's original.

## User Management & Access
- [Overview](docs/features/user-management/index.md): Explains how users are created, imported, disabled and given organizations, the two password policies, password resets, and what the platform records about accounts. Read when you administer users, need to know what disabling or removing a user does, or debug a refused password.
- [Authorization & Roles](docs/features/user-management/authorization.md): The canonical role-gate matrix of the v1 API, the role catalog and who may grant each role, the checks handlers make beyond role gates, and how the admin app gates its pages. Read when you need to know which role opens an endpoint or a page, grant a role, or add a gate to new code.
- [Workflow Type Visibility](docs/features/user-management/workflow-type-visibility.md): Explains the per-user workflow-type visibility filter: a display shortlist that narrows pickers and report lists without changing access. Read when a user cannot find a workflow type in a picker or a run in the Reports list, or when you set a user's shortlist.
- [Stored Keys](docs/features/user-management/stored-keys.md): Explains stored keys: per-organization API keys that a Web API Call header names with {StoredKey.Name}, so the key stays out of the workflow, its run records and its downloads. Read when you give a workflow a third-party API key, rotate one, or debug a web API call that fails on a missing or unreadable key.
- [Multi-Factor Authentication](docs/features/user-management/mfa.md): Explains the two-step MFA sign-in, its factors (TOTP, email code, recovery code, trusted device), the brute-force lockout, the 2FA management endpoints and their errors, and the TwoFactor settings. Read when you turn on or support two-factor sign-in, debug a refused code or a locked account, or script the MFA step.
- [SSO / OIDC](docs/features/user-management/sso-oidc.md): Explains OIDC SSO sign-in (Okta, Auth0, Azure AD, Keycloak) for the SPA and the admin app: the token exchange, how an account is matched, the settings, identity provider setup and every refusal. Read when you set up SSO for a deployment, debug a refused SSO sign-in, or add users who sign in through SSO.

## Glossary
- [Glossary (overview)](docs/reference/glossary.md): Defines core platform terms in plain language: counterparty (shown on screen as Company), RAG, overview, citation, workflow type, run, block, section, document class, report, signature field, tenant. Read when a term in another page is unclear or you need the word the platform uses for a concept.

## API — Core
- [API Overview](docs/reference/api/index.md): Indexes every v1 REST API endpoint by feature area, transcribed from controller route attributes, with the request headers, the tenant checks every request passes, the error format and where the OpenAPI document is served. Read when you look for the endpoint that does something, or need to know why a request answered 401, 403 or 400.
- [Authentication](docs/reference/api/authentication.md): The OAuth 2.0 token endpoint: the password, client-credentials, refresh, Google and OIDC grants, the MFA step, the claims a token carries, every error the endpoint returns, and token lifetimes. Read when you sign in to the API from code, decode a token's claims, or debug a refused sign-in.
- [System Users (Provisioning)](docs/reference/api/system-users.md): Explains how a system user is seeded for each organization, where an integrator's client_id and client_secret come from, which role-gated endpoints a system user reaches, and how to rotate the secret. Read when you hand API credentials to an integrator, stand up a deployment, or wonder why a service login cannot reach an endpoint.
- [Discovery](docs/reference/api/discovery.md): Task flow for discovering the runnable workflow types, their document classes and their variables before a submit. Read when you integrate with the API and need the workflowTypeId, document class keys and variable tags a submit asks for.
- [Users](docs/reference/api/users.md): Documents the Users API: listing an organization's users, discovering the organizations a token can act in, and resolving user names to full names. Read when you list users from code, pick the X-Tenant-Id to send, or show the analyst names on a report list.

## API — Workflows
- [Submit Workflow Execution](docs/reference/api/submit-workflow-execution.md): Documents POST /workflow-executions/submit, the single-call multipart endpoint for integrations, and the calls that follow it: polling the state, reading block status, downloading outputs and the executed workflow, and cancelling. Read when you integrate a service that starts runs with files, or debug a refused submit.
- [Workflow Executions](docs/reference/api/workflow-executions.md): Documents the Workflow Executions API: starting a run, its lifecycle and cancellation, the freeze option that replays another execution's external fetches, logs, the re-run check, and run evidence. Read when you start, cancel or inspect a run from code, read its logs or agent traces, or re-run a report.
- [Reports](docs/reference/api/reports.md): Documents the Workflow Reports API: listing executions, reading one with its documents, reading, editing, deleting and exporting a report's section/paragraph tree, reading the JSON data outputs a run returns beside its report, a run's cost, and the feedback readers leave on a report. Read when you read a run's result, its report or its JSON data from code, export a report to Word or Markdown, or handle report feedback.
- [Background Jobs](docs/reference/api/background-jobs.md): Reference for the read-only Jobs API: listing and fetching the caller's own background jobs, the JobDto shape, the state values and the errors. Read when you poll a run's progress through /jobs or wonder why a job is missing from the list.
- [Executed Workflow Download](docs/reference/api/executed-workflow-download.md): Reference for downloading the JSON snapshot of an executed workflow, with its run evidence, by workflow id, execution id or job id; who may download and every error. Read when you script a run's snapshot download, move a run between environments, or debug a 403 on a download.

## API — Documents & Data
- [Documents](docs/reference/api/documents.md): Reference for the Documents API: list, get, patch, soft-delete, bulk-delete, paginated page listings, one page's full text, the text download, standalone processing into pages, and documents from pasted text. Read when you read or manage documents and their pages from code, process an uploaded file without a run, or debug a document endpoint's 403, 404 or 409.
- [Files](docs/reference/api/files.md): Reference for uploading and downloading files: the byte-level intake gate, deduplication, password-protected uploads, the download headers and every error. Read when you upload or download a document's bytes from code, or debug a refused upload.
- [Page Image](docs/reference/api/page-image.md): Documents GET /pages/{id}/image: renders a document page as a PNG, returns an image page's original bytes, or returns the page text, with its caching headers and errors. Read when you show a cited page to a user or debug a page preview that does not load.
- [Counterparties](docs/reference/api/counterparties.md): Reference for the Counterparties API: list, the peer candidates for a run, get, create, update, delete, validation rules and errors, the bundle export and import that move an organization's counterparties between instances, and the counterparty type endpoints. Read when you create or sync counterparties from code, move them between instances, or debug a 400 or 409 from a counterparty write.

## Database Schema
- [Overview](docs/reference/database/index.md): Overviews the two databases, Core and UserData: what each holds, how tenant data is scoped, the providers, and how migrations run. Read when you need to know which schema holds a table, or how the databases are created and migrated.
- [Core Database](docs/reference/database/core-database.md): Lists the Core schema column by column: workflow templates, sections, blocks, versioning, the Library, signature overrides, stored keys, model pricing, validation schemas and the AI prompt tables. Read when you query or migrate the Core database or need the stored shape of a template table.
- [User Data Database](docs/reference/database/user-data-database.md): Documents every table of the UserData schema — executed workflows, runs, documents, counterparties, reports, agent runs, validation, monitoring, regression, token usage and the framework tables — with its columns, plus how tenant isolation and soft delete work on it. Read when you query or migrate UserData tables, or need to know where a run, a document or a user's data is stored.

## Deployment & CI/CD
- [Release Package Deployment](docs/operations/release-package-deployment.md): Customer-facing runbook for a deployment in the customer's own environment: what a release contains, how to obtain the images, host sizing, the secrets and TLS the operator supplies, bring-up on one Docker host, health checks, upgrades and rollback. Read when you deploy, upgrade or roll back the platform from release images in your own environment.
- [First Login](docs/operations/first-login.md): Final deployment step: the two seeded admin accounts and where their passwords come from, which URL to open for the analyst app and the admin app, the signed-in check, and login troubleshooting with the exact startup errors. Read when a fresh deployment is up and nobody has signed in yet, or a first sign-in fails.
- [Customer-Owned Bedrock Setup](docs/operations/customer-bedrock-setup.md): Production checklist for pointing a deployment at the customer's own AWS Bedrock: AWS mode, the IAM policy for Claude and the Cohere embeddings, the instance profile, the region, console model access, the agent runtime's own role, and the post-deploy AI smoke test. Read when a self-hosted deployment will call Bedrock in the customer's AWS account, or a Bedrock call fails with AccessDenied.
- [Application Configuration](docs/operations/application-configuration.md): Reference of the runtime configuration keys of the API and admin apps: how the sources layer, connection strings, PlatformSettings and its subsections, authentication, JWT, file storage, email, data protection, logging and CORS, each with a placeholder value. Read when you configure a deployment, look up what a key does or its default, or a startup error names a configuration key.
- [Calling an Internal Service](docs/operations/internal-service-calls.md): The process a deployment follows before a workflow may call an internal service: request, review, approval, the change, verification and the record of every exception. Read when a workflow's Web API Call or an email link is refused with \"Refused to connect\", or someone asks to let workflows reach a service inside a deployment's network.

## Reliability & Security
- [Soft-Delete Cleanup](docs/operations/soft-delete-cleanup.md): How the background service hard-deletes expired soft-deleted UserData records on a per-org schedule: the schedule and settings, the ordered delete, the rows with no foreign key, the Core purge of retired workflow types, configuration, the schema drift tests and the log lines. Read when soft-deleted data must go or must stay, a deleted workflow type must go, you add a UserData table or foreign key, or the cleanup's schema test fails.

## Compliance
